R-01.title: Quotes not sought for payments just below the quotation thresholds
R-01.statement: Payments sitting just below a quotation threshold may indicate that the quotes the Rules require were not sought [rule:CPR-53] [rule:CPR-54].
R-01.lj: Weak signal. Just below the £{{$.thresholds[1].value}} threshold there are {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[1].band_count}} payments [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[1].band_count] against {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[1].comparator_count}} just above it [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[1].comparator_count], so there is no excess below the line, and only {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[1].by_tag.general_procurement.rows}} of them are general procurement [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[1].by_tag.general_procurement.rows]. Below £{{$.thresholds[0].value}} the band count of {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[0].band_count}} [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[0].band_count] exceeds the {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[0].comparator_count}} above [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[0].comparator_count], but that band includes payments of exactly the threshold value and the rule there asks for a single quote [rule:CPR-53]. No payment falls in the band below the next threshold up [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[2].band_count]. Contract Letting received Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-01], so no uplift.
R-01.ij: The general-procurement value in the band below the three-quote threshold, £{{$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[1].by_tag.general_procurement.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.per_threshold[1].by_tag.general_procurement.gbp], falls in the Medium financial band [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[2].financial]; the three-quote and contract notice duties are mandatory [rule:CPR-54]. No adjustment.
R-01.focus: For the general-procurement payments in the band just below the three-quote threshold, check that invitations to quote went to at least three sources through the Procurement Portal and that a contract notice was published.
R-01.scope_reason: Auditor: "Bring into scope. Threshold-hugging at the £{{$.thresholds[1].value}} quote boundary is a standard test and cheap to sample; keep the rating as it is."

R-02.title: Requirements split into payments that each stay under the quotation threshold
R-02.statement: Repeated payments to one supplier that each stay under a quotation threshold but together cross it may indicate a requirement split to avoid competition [rule:CPR-10].
R-02.lj: Clear signal: {{$.tests.split_purchases.per_threshold[0].headline_general_procurement.windows}} general-procurement windows (one per supplier) where two or more payments each under £{{$.thresholds[1].value}} reach it within {{$.tests.split_purchases.parameters.window_days}} days [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.per_threshold[0].headline_general_procurement.windows], well over a handful of suppliers. Held at 3 rather than 4 because regular payments under one existing contract produce the same pattern and the published data cannot tell the two apart. Placement windows ({{$.tests.split_purchases.per_threshold[0].care_or_education_placement.windows}}) are left out because periodic care fees legitimately recur [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.per_threshold[0].care_or_education_placement.windows]. Counts are lower bounds since payments of the publication floor or less are not published [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.parameters.lower_bound_note]. Fraud and financial control are a named source of risk [history:RT-02]; no adverse audit on the theme, so no uplift.
R-02.ij: The flagged general-procurement total of £{{$.tests.split_purchases.per_threshold[0].headline_general_procurement.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.per_threshold[0].headline_general_procurement.gbp] falls in the Critical financial band [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[0].financial]. Reduced by one point: the total is the value of the windows, not a loss, and a split below the quotation threshold matches the Major compliance descriptor, a high possibility of legal challenge [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[1].compliance] [rule:CPR-10].
R-02.focus: For a sample of general-procurement windows, establish whether the payments relate to one requirement; where they do, check the competition the combined value required was run, or that an existing contract covers them.
R-02.scope_reason: Clear signal across many suppliers on a mandatory anti-avoidance rule.

R-03.title: High-value awards made without Key Decision or the approvals in Appendix A
R-03.statement: Awards above the Key Decision threshold that do not follow the approval route in Appendix A may indicate contracts awarded outside delegated authority [rule:CPR-02] [rule:CPR-51] [rule:CPR-52].
R-03.lj: The award approval record is not in the published data, so the control cannot be observed directly. The only data signal is weak: {{$.tests.split_purchases.per_threshold[1].headline_general_procurement.windows}} general-procurement windows where payments each under £{{$.thresholds[2].value}} reach that value within {{$.tests.split_purchases.parameters.window_days}} days [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.per_threshold[1].headline_general_procurement.windows]. No audit in the papers covers award approvals, so no adverse history. The council's compliance appetite names high value transactions [history:RT-08].
R-03.ij: The flagged windows total £{{$.tests.split_purchases.per_threshold[1].headline_general_procurement.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.per_threshold[1].headline_general_procurement.gbp], in the Critical financial band [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[0].financial]; an award that should have been a Key Decision but was not carries a probable legal challenge [rule:CPR-02]. No adjustment.
R-03.focus: For the general-procurement windows reaching the Key Decision threshold and the largest annualised suppliers, trace the award to its approval: Key Decision record, board-approved report and the recommendations Appendix A requires.
R-03.scope_reason: Small population with Critical exposure; the approval route is the control the data cannot see.

R-04.title: Spend above the quotation threshold with no published contract notice
R-04.statement: Suppliers paid at or above the quotation threshold on an annualised basis with no matching published contract notice may indicate spend without the competition or notice the Rules require [rule:CPR-54]. This covers general procurement, grants, which the Rules treat as contracts [rule:CPR-66], and agency staff, a bought service. The notice export is not a contract register, so this is an indicator to check, not evidence of off-contract spend.
R-04.lj: At or above £{{$.tests.off_contract.parameters.threshold}} annualised with no exact-name match to an active notice there are {{$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.general_procurement.suppliers}} general-procurement suppliers [metric:$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.general_procurement.suppliers], {{$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.grant.suppliers}} grant suppliers [metric:$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.grant.suppliers] and a further {{$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.agency_staff.suppliers}} in agency staff [metric:$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.agency_staff.suppliers], against {{$.tests.off_contract.per_match_class.exact.suppliers}} exact matches across all tags [metric:$.tests.off_contract.per_match_class.exact.suppliers]: a clear signal by count. Grants come within the Rules because providing funding or a grant to an external organisation is entering a contract [rule:CPR-66]. Held at 3 because the source holds published notices only and no contract register was available [metric:$.tests.off_contract.register_present]; earlier awards, notices placed elsewhere, framework call-offs under another buyer and grant agreements not published as notices will not appear. Placement suppliers stay with R-09 because placements are exempt from competition [rule:CPR-64]; premises costs are left out as property costs, not purchases under the Rules. Contract Letting received Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-01], so no uplift. Adding grants and agency staff does not move the score.
R-04.ij: The annualised estimate for unmatched general-procurement suppliers alone, £{{$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.general_procurement.annualised_estimate_gbp}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.general_procurement.annualised_estimate_gbp], is in the Critical financial band [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[0].financial]; unmatched grant suppliers add £{{$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.grant.annualised_estimate_gbp}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.grant.annualised_estimate_gbp] and agency-staff suppliers £{{$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.agency_staff.annualised_estimate_gbp}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.agency_staff.annualised_estimate_gbp]. Competition and publication duties apply [rule:CPR-54] [rule:CPR-05], to grants as to other contracts [rule:CPR-66]. Already at the top of the scale, so the wider population does not move the score. No adjustment.
R-04.focus: Obtain the council's contract register and grant agreements and reconcile them to the unmatched general-procurement, grant and agency-staff suppliers, confirming near matches first; for suppliers still unmatched, request the quote, tender, grant award or waiver record behind the spend.
R-04.scope_reason: Largest exposure in the register; the reconciliation also tests register completeness, the reason R-10 was rejected.

R-05.title: Duplicate or repeated payments of the same amount
R-05.statement: Payments to the same supplier for the same amount within seven days may indicate duplicate or repeated payment without separate evidence of purchase [rule:CPR-29].
R-05.lj: Clear signal in general procurement: {{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.same_timestamp.by_tag.general_procurement.groups}} groups share an identical payment date [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.same_timestamp.by_tag.general_procurement.groups] and {{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.groups}} more fall on different dates within seven days [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.groups]. Placement groups ({{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.same_timestamp.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.groups}} same-date, {{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.groups}} different-date) [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.same_timestamp.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.groups] are not counted towards the score because fees at a standard rate legitimately repeat across service users. Accounts Payable received Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-15], so no uplift.
R-05.ij: The general-procurement value beyond the first payment in the different-date tier, £{{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp_beyond_first}} [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp_beyond_first], is in the Medium financial band [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[2].financial]; the same-date tier adds a smaller £{{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.same_timestamp.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp_beyond_first}} [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.same_timestamp.by_tag.general_procurement.gbp_beyond_first]. This is within the council's stated financial appetite range [history:RT-07]. No adjustment.
R-05.focus: For a sample of general-procurement groups, match each payment to a distinct invoice and purchase record, and confirm any true duplicate was recovered; include a few of the largest placement groups to confirm they relate to different service users.
R-05.scope_reason: Clear signal with a direct test against invoices.

R-06.title: Spend continuing after the published contract has ended
R-06.statement: Payments to suppliers whose only published contract notices ended before the spend window may indicate spend continuing after expiry without an approved extension [rule:CPR-61].
R-06.lj: Weak signal: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.suppliers}} suppliers [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.suppliers], and a newer contract may exist with no notice [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.caveat]. Contract management is a named source of risk [history:RT-03]; no adverse audit on the theme, so no uplift.
R-06.ij: The annualised estimate of £{{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.annualised_estimate_gbp}} [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.annualised_estimate_gbp] falls in the Major financial band [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[1].financial]. Reduced by one point: a missing extension approval matches the Medium compliance descriptor, a reasonable possibility of legal challenge [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[2].compliance] [rule:CPR-61]; the window total of £{{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.gbp}} [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.gbp] includes one-off payments that annualising overstates.
R-06.focus: For each flagged supplier, obtain the current contract or the S151-approved extension covering the payments in the window.

R-07.title: Spend running above the awarded contract value without an approved variation
R-07.statement: Annualised spend well above a contract's awarded annual rate may indicate a variation of scope or value without the approval the Rules require [rule:CPR-62] [rule:CPR-63].
R-07.lj: Clear signal: {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.flagged}} of {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.suppliers_assessed}} assessed suppliers have an annualised estimate at least {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.parameters.ratio_flag}} times the award's annual rate [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.flagged] [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.suppliers_assessed], more than a handful. Award values may be estimates or maxima [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.caveat]. Contract management is a named source of risk [history:RT-03]; no adverse audit on the theme, so no uplift.
R-07.ij: The flagged annualised estimate of £{{$.tests.spend_vs_award.flagged_annualised_estimate_gbp}} [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.flagged_annualised_estimate_gbp] is in the Critical financial band [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[0].financial]. Reduced by one point: the exposure is the excess over each award, which is smaller than the flagged total, and an unapproved variation matches the Major compliance descriptor [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[1].compliance] [rule:CPR-63].
R-07.focus: For each flagged supplier, compare spend to the signed contract value and obtain any variation approval; confirm whether the published award value was an estimate or a maximum.
R-07.scope_reason: Clear signal across a defined population of matched contracts.

R-08.title: Waivers and exceptions granted without the required approval
R-08.statement: Competition may be waived or an exception applied without the documentation and approval the Rules require; the Rules name different approvers for a waiver [rule:CPR-17] [rule:CPR-18].
R-08.lj: The waiver and exception record is not in the published data, so the control cannot be observed; no audit in the papers covers waivers, so no adverse history and no uplift. The Rules conflict on who may waive: the relevant Executive Director or Chief Executive under one clause [rule:CPR-17], only the Monitoring Officer or S151 Officer under another [rule:CPR-18], which makes a wrongly authorised waiver harder to spot.
R-08.ij: No exposure in pounds can be measured for waivers. Rated on the compliance descriptor: a waiver approved by the wrong officer or left undocumented gives a reasonable possibility of successful legal challenge, the Medium descriptor [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[2].compliance]; every waiver must be documented and approved by the S151 Officer [rule:CPR-22] [rule:CPR-24].
R-08.focus: Obtain the waiver and exception log for the window, check each entry for documentation, advance approval by the correct officer and a board report where required, and ask which approver the council treats as authoritative.
R-08.scope_reason: Mandatory control the data cannot see, with conflicting approver wording in the Rules.

R-09.title: Care and education placements without the recorded reasons for provider choice
R-09.statement: Care and education placements, which are exempt from competition, may be made without the reasons for the choice of provider recorded on the case notes as the Rules require [rule:CPR-64].
R-09.lj: Case notes are not in the spend data, so the control cannot be observed: base score 2. The {{$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.care_or_education_placement.suppliers}} placement suppliers paid at or above the quotation threshold with no notice [metric:$.tests.off_contract.unmatched_by_dominant_tag.care_or_education_placement.suppliers] are expected under the exemption and are not read as a signal. Purchase of Residential and Nursing Care received Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-18]. Raised to 3 by the repeat-finding uplift below.
R-09.ij: Placement spend in the window, £{{$.population.tags.care_or_education_placement.gbp}} [metric:$.population.tags.care_or_education_placement.gbp], is in the Critical financial band [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[0].financial]. Reduced by one point: the duty at stake is a recording requirement under an exemption, nearer the Major compliance descriptor than probable regulatory intervention [history:$.scoring_method.impact_scale[1].compliance] [rule:CPR-64].
R-09.focus: For a sample of placement payments, check that the case notes record the reasons for the provider chosen and, where the Provider Selection Regime applies, that its process was followed.
R-09.scope_reason: Adverse audit on the theme and the largest tagged spend population.

uplift.justification: Personal Budgets (Direct Payments) received Limited Assurance in the latest completed-work appendix [history:AUD-16]; direct payments fall within this theme of care purchased outside the Rules, so likelihood is raised by one point.
